Reviews of the latest Hunger Games film have seen it dismissed as a "surreally awful prequel" and "a tortuous, costly mess" by some critics - but called "surprisingly strong" and "one of the best films in the series" by others.
The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is the sixth movie in the franchise, and tells the origin story of a teenage Haymitch Abernathy - who was played as an adult by Woody Harrelson.
In a one-star review, the Guardian called the film , external "overwrought and boring", and said it "has no actual interest and no authentic reason to exist, other than to gouge an income stream out of its fanbase".
But the Wrap praised its , external "memorable performances, intoxicating style and horrifying commentary", adding: "When the dust settles it may even be the Hunger Games that holds up best."
Sunrise on the Reaping is set 24 years before the first Hunger Games film, and 40 years after the previous prequel, 2023's The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes.
"This prequel lands at some mid-point between Ballad and Hunger Games, which puts it on an immediately odd footing," Empire said in a three-star review , external .
"It can't escape the sense of feeling supplementary. It's an enjoyable-enough diversion, but essentially a footnote with aspirations."
Screen Daily called it , external an "underwhelming prequel", which "suffers from a lack of compelling characters" and "feels oddly incidental - a drab afterthought rather than a crucial new chapter".
The film's all-star cast includes Ralph Fiennes, Jesse Plemons, Glenn Close, Kieran Culkin, Elle Fanning, Mckenna Grace and Maya Hawke alongside Joseph Zada as the 16-year-old Abernathy.
IndieWire , external said Zada's performance is "charming enough", but "his character lacks the gravitational charisma or arc that, say, Jennifer Lawrence brought to the original films".
The movie feels "a little bit like a cold cash grab rather than a necessary deepening of the series' lore" and is "a dreary slog", IndieWire's critic wrote.
The New York Times , external also used the word "slog", adding: "One really misses the guiding presence of Jennifer Lawrence, who had the raw pathos to both ground and expand a world in a way many younger stars often can't.
"In Sunrise, we're instead left with fleeting moments in which Plemons or Ralph Fiennes (playing the evil President Snow) briefly elevate the film. They seem to be trapped in this dystopia too."
The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping will be released this weekend
However, the Hollywood Reporter , external was more enthusiastic about both the film and Zada's performance, calling it a "star-making turn".
Its critic concluded: "Sunrise on the Reaping is a return, after the disappointing Songbirds and Snakes, to the spirit of the first movies."
And Time Out's four-star review , external said the film is "as strong as any" of the other movies, and "certainly a major step up from 2023's drab prequel The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes".

Avustralya 'ya bağlı Christmas Adası'nda on milyonlarca kırmızı yengeç, her yıl olduğu gibi ormanlardan denize doğru göçe başladı. 14 ve 15 Kasım'da yollar ve yengeçler için yapılan geçitler kırmızıya büründü.
Göç genellikle ekim ya da kasımda başlıyor, bazı yıllarda aralık hatta ocak ayına kadar sarkabiliyor. Bu yıl da yoğun yağışların ardından adanın dört bir yanındaki yengeçler aynı anda yuvalarından çıkıp kıyıya doğru yürümeye başladı.
Görüntülerde yengeçlerin yolları geçtiği, üst geçitlere tırmandığı ve kendilerini yönlendiren bariyerleri takip ettiği görülüyor.
Göçü yöneten Avustralya Milli Parklar İdaresi'nin ekipleri alt geçitleri temizliyor, yolların üzerine özel yengeç köprüleri kuruyor ve yengeçleri trafikten uzak tutmak için yol kenarlarına kilometrelerce bariyer yerleştiriyor.
Göçün en yoğun olduğu dönemde bazı yollar, çoğu zaman kısa süre önce haber verilerek günün bir kısmında ya da tamamında trafiğe kapatılıyor. Ziyaretçiler ise arabalarını park edip yengeçlerin arasında dikkatle yürüyebiliyor.
Kırmızı yengeçler, Ay'ın son dördün evresinde, şafaktan önce yüksek gelgitin çekilmeye başladığı sırada yumurtalarını denize bırakıyor.
Yağmur bu tarihe yakın başlarsa yengeçler yetişmek için hızlanıyor. Yağmur çok geç gelirse bazıları yuvasında kalıp göçü bir sonraki aya erteliyor.
Kıyıya önce iri erkek yengeçler ulaşıyor ve adanın alçak teraslarında yuva kazıyor; yuva için birbirleriyle kavga etmeleri de sık görülüyor. Çiftleşmenin ardından erkekler geri dönüyor, dişiler ise yumurtalar gelişene kadar yaklaşık iki hafta yuvada kalıyor.
Çoğu yıl denizden karaya neredeyse hiç yavru yengeç dönmüyor. Ancak on yılda bir ya da iki kez çok sayıda yavru hayatta kalıyor ve bu, adadaki büyük yengeç nüfusunu korumaya yetiyor.

We have barely come up for breath since Robert Pattinson was picked as the new James Bond, but A-listers are already jostling for position to play his enemy in the next 007 movie.
At the premiere of his new film in Hollywood on Monday, Brad Pitt was asked by Extra TV , external if he would like to play the villain in director Denis Villeneuve's forthcoming spy movie.
With a wink at the camera, the star replied: "Robert! Denis! You know, I'd like to do that. I'd be up for that. My man Javier [Bardem] did it so well. It's tall shoes, but I'd take that on."
Bardem played Bond baddie Raoul Silva in 2012's Skyfall, opposite Daniel Craig. Asked the same question by Complex , external later, Pitt was still enthusiastic: "Sign me up for the villain. Get Denis Villeneuve on the flip phone, let's go!"
Florence Pugh was presented with an award by Dune: Part 3 and James Bond director Denis Villeneuve on Monday
Meanwhile, Florence Pugh, who stars alongside Pattinson in Villeneuve's forthcoming Dune: Part Three, said she had thrown her hat in the ring to be in the new Bond film upon hearing the casting news.
Speaking at Elle's Women in Hollywood event on Monday, Pugh said she had sent a message to the director saying: "Congratulations on finding your Bond, nice catch. Any villains the size of a 5ft 4in female?"
In fact, it was Villeneuve presenting Pugh with an honour at the event - so he's now heard her plea twice.
Meanwhile, Pitt also told reporters at the premiere of The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth in Los Angeles that he was delighted to hear the news about Pattinson's recruitment as 007.
"Is that right?! You know what, I love this idea," Pitt told Extra TV.
"I love what he's been doing. I love his choices, I think he's the real deal. That's great, good call."
Bond villains over the years have included Rami Malek, Jonathan Pryce, Christoph Waltz and Christopher Walken.
Several other actors have indicated they would like a shot at being a Bond baddie ahead of Pattinson's casting announcement, including Bill Skarsgård, Saoirse Ronan and Barry Keoghan.

The US has lost its measles-free status, international health officials said Tuesday, as the highly contagious virus has spread at the fastest rate in more than 30 years, while Mexico and Bolivia also lost their measles-elimination status. Vaccination rates have been falling against a number of diseases, in the US and globally, and measles has been spreading throughout the Americas since 2024.
The US has lost its measles-free status, international health officials said Tuesday, as the highly contagious virus once relegated to medical textbooks has spread – largely among the unvaccinated – at the highest rate in more than 30 years.
Mexico also lost its measles-elimination status, following a resurgence of the virus there that included a massive outbreak in Chihuahua state. Bolivia , too, lost its status.
The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) declaration has few practical implications and is largely symbolic, but it marks a sharp turnabout in a disease largely controlled through decades of scientific advances. It also may be seen as the beginning of an era in which diseases of the past become deadly problems for the modern world.
“Measles elimination is not a trophy that is won once and placed on a shelf,” Dr. Jarbas Barbosa, PAHO’s director, said at a news conference. “It is an achievement that must be safeguarded every day by closing immunity gaps and ensuring we reach every community.”
PAHO expects the US, Bolivia and Mexico to submit plans "in the coming weeks” for how each country will go about trying to stop transmission for at least a year and regain measles elimination status, Dr. Daniel Salas, the organization's executive manager for immunisations, told reporters.
Measles has been spreading throughout the Americas since 2024. The outbreaks in North America started in close-knit Mennonite communities and have since spread to areas with low vaccination rates. Last year, Canada lost its measles-free designation for the first time since 1998 .
International health officials consider measles eliminated when the virus is not locally spreading among residents. The designation hinges on whether a single measles chain has spread uninterrupted for at least 12 months.
Tuesday's announcement signals an erosion of public health preparedness.
Vaccination rates have been falling against a number of diseases , in the US and globally. And as one of the most infectious diseases known to medicine, measles was seen as likely to be one of the first vaccine-preventable diseases to reemerge when vaccinations falter.
“It can be the canary in the coal mine to other things,” said Dr. Susan Kansagra, chief medical officer of the Association of State and Territorial Health Officials.
Measles vaccine have safely stopped the virus’ spread in the US for 30 years.
It takes a community vaccination rate of 95% to prevent outbreaks, experts say. But as fewer parents vaccinate their children and federal leaders sow doubt and confusion about the importance of getting vaccinated, the virus has found footholds in communities across the US. All but three states have reported a confirmed case of measles this year.

The illness typically begins with a high fever followed by a telltale rash that starts on the face and neck. Most people recover, but it’s one of the leading causes of death among young children, according to the World Health Organization. Serious complications, including blindness and swelling of the brain, are more common in young children and adults over age 30.
Ten measles-associated deaths have been reported in the US this year, making it the deadliest in more than three decades. Health officials haven't released detailed information on each death, but at least five of the dead were children.
Since the US eliminated measles in 2000, public health officials usually logged fewer than 200 cases a year, most of them tied to international travel.
But since 2025, measles has sickened thousands. It started with a major outbreak in the Southwest.
In Texas, more than 760 people got sick and two children died . In New Mexico, about 100 people got sick and one adult died. Then measles exploded in rural border towns in Arizona and Utah, followed by a major outbreak in South Carolina in the winter and spring that sickened nearly 1,000 people.
This year has been much worse – the worst for measles cases since 1991. The more than 5,400 confirmed cases so far this year are already double the 2025 tally, driven largely by an outbreak in Pennsylvania that dwarfed the earlier ones.
And the outbreak tallies are almost certainly an undercount, public health experts say.
US Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. was a leading voice in the anti-vaccine movement before US President Donald Trump appointed him to oversee federal health agencies.
Kennedy and other federal leaders have argued that vaccination rates were waning for years before Trump took office a second time, that measles is not an “American phenomenon", and that the US government is handling measles better than other countries. In January, a US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) leader told reporters that the loss of the nation's elimination status would be the “cost of doing business” globally.
It's true that other countries are struggling with measles, and some also have lost their measles-elimination status. But public health experts and others say the outcome in the US wasn't inevitable.
“This humiliating determination is the tragic yet predictable result of an ongoing campaign by grifters, quacks and charlatans to put their own greed and self-worth ahead of the health and safety of children,” said Senator Ron Wyden, a Democrat from Oregon.
The government has been taking some steps. In August and September, the CDC awarded $100 million to support state and local measles-response work. And Kennedy and CDC Director Dr. Erica Schwartz have made statements that vaccination is the best way to prevent measles from spreading.

“The measles elimination designation is not what protects Americans. Vaccination does,” Schwartz said in a statement Tuesday. "We know where transmission is occurring and we’ve invested $100 million in state and local health departments to reach those communities.”
But state and local health officials say the cost is far higher and that the moment demands a louder federal voice – and a bigger push for vaccinations – than Kennedy and Schwartz are providing.
“When the people at the front of the room are not speaking loudly and frequently in support of vaccination, the program starts to falter. And that’s what we’re seeing in the US,” said Noel Brewer, a University of North Carolina public health professor who chairs a committee that presented an analysis of US measles data to PAHO last week. “How many kids have to die before they start getting concerned?”
Some experts noted that neither Kennedy nor the CDC has scheduled a news conference to address their plans to fight measles. When the AP asked for Kennedy’s reaction to the US losing its measles-free status, an HHS spokesperson pointed to Schwartz’s statement. Projenin yönetmen koltuğunda Zeynep Günay oturacak. Senaryoyu ise Nükhet Bıçakçı kaleme alıyor. Senaryo, yönetmen ve yapımcı kadrosu belli olan projede sıra oyuncu seçimine geldi.
Dizinin yeni yılda ekrana gelmesi hedefleniyor. Ancak Nilüfer'in hangi kanalda yayınlanacağı henüz netleşmedi.
Dizinin hikâyesi, memleketine başsavcı olarak dönen Nilüfer Ölmez'in etrafında şekilleniyor. Doğduğu topraklara bu kez yasanın temsilcisi olarak dönen Nilüfer'in yolu, ağa ailesinin oğlu Aslan'la kesişecek. Bir yanda hukuku temsil eden bir başsavcı, diğer yanda ağa ailesinin oğlu... İki karakter arasındaki ilişki hikâyenin merkezinde yer alacak.

Mardin 'de geçen Hercai'den Antep'te başlayan Yalı Çapkını'na kadar pek çok yapım, Anadolu'daki köklü aile hikâyeleriyle izleyiciden karşılık buldu. Nilüfer ise bu kez hikâyeyi bir kadın başsavcının gözünden anlatacak. Gaziantep 'te çekilmesi planlanan sahneler, hikâyenin geçtiği coğrafyayı da ekrana taşıyacak.
Nilüfer karakterine hangi oyuncunun hayat vereceği ise henüz açıklanmadı.
Dizinin erkek başrolü Aslan için ise dikkat çekici bir isim gündemde. Kulislerden aktarılan bilgilere göre yapım ekibi, Aslan karakteri için Burak Deniz ile görüşüyor. Görüşmeler olumlu sonuçlanırsa ünlü oyuncu, final yapan Sahtekarlar'ın ardından yeni bir projeyle ekranlara dönmüş olacak. Yapım şirketinden konuya ilişkin henüz resmi bir açıklama gelmedi.
Aşk Laftan Anlamaz, Maraşlı ve Bambaşka Biri gibi dizilerle geniş bir hayran kitlesi edinen Burak Deniz'in bir aşiret hikâyesinde ağa oğlu rolüne bürünme ihtimali şimdiden merak konusu oldu.
Başsavcı Nilüfer'in karşısında hikâyenin diğer ucunda yer alacak Aslan, dizinin en kritik karakterlerinden biri olacak.
Peki Burak Deniz, Nilüfer'in Aslan'ı olacak mı? Dizinin kadrosu ve yayınlanacağı kanalla ilgili gelişmeler önümüzdeki günlerde netleşecek.

Hollandalı Loop Biotech şirketi, mantarların toprak altındaki ipliksi yapısı olan miselyumdan tabut üretiyor. Şirket, bu tabutların uygun koşullarda toprağa gömüldükten yaklaşık 45 gün sonra çözündüğünü ve toprağı beslediğini söylüyor. Gelin birlikte bakalım.
Living Cocoon adı verilen tabut, Delft'teki iklim kontrollü bir odada kalıp içinde yetiştiriliyor ve yaklaşık yedi günde hazır hâle geliyor. Üretimde kimyasal, yapıştırıcı ya da metal kullanılmıyor.
Tabutun içi standart olarak yosunla kaplanıyor, istenirse başka doğal malzemeler de kullanılabiliyor.
Mantar tabut ise uygun koşullarda yaklaşık 45 günde çözünüyor. Bu süreç kompostlamaya benziyor; tabut ve beden yavaş yavaş besin açısından zengin toprağa dönüşüyor.
Tabut yalnızca toprakla temas ettiğinde çözünmeye başladığı için cenaze gününe kadar kuru ve havadar bir yerde saklanabiliyor.
30 kilo gelen tabut, 200 kiloya kadar taşıyabiliyor ve altı kişinin omuzlayabilmesi için altı jüt sapı bulunuyor. Dayanıklılık ve suya karşı direnç testlerinden geçen tabut için cenaze evlerinin ek bir düzenleme yapmasına gerek kalmıyor.
Fiyatı 3.995 dolar olan tabut Hollanda dışında da kullanılmaya başladı. Avustralya 'nın Yeni Güney Galler eyaletinde 70'li yaşlarındaki bir kadın bu tabutla toprağa verildi.

Late-night hosts discussed the administration’s unhelpful response to the FAA’s rare ground stop this weekend
Late-night hosts responded to the FAA’s sudden, rare ground stop as Donald Trump shirks any responsibility for the transportation crisis.
Jon Stewart opened Monday’s Daily Show with a recap of the Federal Aviation Administration’s shock ground stoppage on Friday afternoon, which stranded travelers across the country and led to cascading delays. Stewart had particular ire for the homeland security secretary, Markwayne Mullin, who comforted worried travelers on Friday evening with: “This isn’t another 9/11.”
“Who said 9/11! Why would you bring up 9/11?!” Stewart marveled. “These motherfuckers just want to know if they’re going to miss their connecting flights!”
Later in his press conference, as the crisis was still unfolding, Mullin took the time to correct a reporter who asked if the stoppage was related to an AI error – “We call it SI [super intelligence] around here, remember?” he said.
“That’s your problem?” Stewart mocked. “Deadnaming the robots? You just invoked 9/11, and now you’re the grammar police? ‘Uh, excuse me, miss, the planes will be crashing into the Gulf of America .’
“This is so chaotic and amateurish – which makes sense,” he added. As Mullin said, “This is what the leadership of President Trump looks like.”
And “while it may feel like all of our nation’s critical systems are falling apart, each one on a different day, like an advent calendar of societal collapse, help is on the way,” Stewart added, referring to the rumored comeback of the disgraced Nvidia CEO, Jensen Huang, following his affair with a suspected Chinese spy.
“A comeback? Oh, it’s been a long weekend,” Stewart quipped. “What’d you do, one day of soul-searching per affair? A comeback? How is this even possible?” Stewart then cut to a clip of Trump saying that he “would not mind” Huang’s reinstatement at Nvidia because “he’s a great, brilliant person, and we want to protect our brilliant people.”
“The entire Jensen Huang soap opera exposes how all of these tech titans have us normies by the short and curlies,” said Stewart. “Like they’re creating the most powerful technology that the world has ever seen. Even they say in their filing to go public could pose an existential threat to humanity, but we are not even allowed to regulate them.”
“Sometimes it feels like maybe Elon and his Doge bros shouldn’t have fired more than a thousand employees at the FAA,” said Jimmy Kimmel on Monday evening, as US air travel still faced numerous delays and cancellations.
“We learned this weekend a very valuable lesson: we learned what happens when the only experience your secretary of transportation has when it comes to transportation is being on Road Rules All Stars on MTV.
“And where, you may ask, was the president during all of this?” Kimmel continued. “He was in the Oval Office meeting with his 87-year-old ambassador to Hollywood, Jon Voight. Trump pulled a real disappearing act on this one. He didn’t post about it Friday or Saturday. But he did find time to complain about the public golf course he’s trying to forcibly renovate in Washington.”
That would be the city’s East Potomac Park and Golf Link, which Trump calls “Trash Island”. Trump wrote on Truth Social: “Trash Island is currently the worst golf course anywhere in the world. The fairways are far too close together. When you walk down the corridors of Trash Island, you don’t hear the sound of the running Potomac. All you hear is the sound of people screaming, ‘FORE!’”
“You might be wondering, with all that’s going on, why the president is posting about ‘Trash Island’,” Kimmel noted. “It’s very simple: Now that he can’t go to Epstein’s island, you know, he needs an island. He needs one island at all times.”
And on Late Night, Seth Meyers skewered Trump’s refusal to engage with the FAA stoppage on any level. As Trump told the press on Monday: “I don’t take any responsibility.”
“No, of course not! Why would you?” Meyers retorted. “The constitution says the president’s only responsibilities are tweets, memes and ballrooms.
“After several days of near silence, the president finally emerged from hiding to explain to a worried nation that the air traffic control system, the one that keeps us all safe while flying, had a heart attack and that’s why he wants to blow it up,” said Meyers of Trump’s eventual comments on the matter to a gaggle of reporters outside the White House. “Is there anything else you’d like to explain to the class before we go to the school board and demand to have you removed?”
Meyers then played a clip of Trump claiming that “the Biden administration hooked up a lot of copper into glass” for the nation’s flight communication system, which was not advised “if you know anything about electrical engineering”.
“Now, if you’re wondering if you cannot hook up copper into glass, the answer is actually yes, he’s correct,” Meyers joked.
“Of course he’s not fucking right!” he added. “You can transmit data from copper to glass the same way Trump transmits data to the media from his ass. Do you seriously think the same oatmeal-brained 80-year-old who once spelled the word tap with two Ps was secretly an electrical engineer this whole time?”

JJ Gabriel has announced his departure from Manchester United by posting a farewell message to the club on social media.
The teenager, who has not played a competitive game for the first team, joined as a 10-year-old in 2020 but has been absent since he requested the cancellation of his registration in September before he turned 16, on 6 October.
It has been widely reported that he will join Real Madrid and while he made no mention of his intended destination, his goodbye video on Instagram appears to have taken him closer to a move to the Spanish giants.
Gabriel said in the video: “Dear Manchester United, I arrived in 2020 as a 10-year-old boy with big dreams. Here I grew as a player and a person. From scoring at Old Trafford to receiving the Jimmy Murphy Award.
“You gave me moments I will always treasure. To every coach and every member of staff, to my teammates and everyone who supported me, thank you for believing in me and helping me grow.
“As I begin my next chapter, Manchester United will always be a part of my story. Thank you for everything, JJ.”
This article includes content provided by Instagram . We ask for your permission before anything is loaded, as they may be using cookies and other technologies. To view this content, click 'Allow and continue' .
Gabriel had remained registered to United, who are understood to be ready to explore legal options against the youngster’s next club over a possible breach of regulations.
The 16-year-old is the son of former Republic of Ireland international, Joe O’Cearuill, and last season became the youngest winner of United’s Jimmy Murphy Award, for their young player of the year.
United had hoped to persuade the teenager to stay but it appears his hat-trick-scoring turn against Sabah on his Uefa Youth League debut, on 10 September, will be his final appearance for the club. Gabriel shone in that 5-0 victory although his representatives were disappointed he was not registered to play later that day in the Champions League fixture against the champions of Azerbaijan.
The teenager was due to appear in the Carabao Cup tie against Brighton the next week but had seemingly decided upon a new direction by that point. Gabriel would have become the club’s youngest player in a competitive match in that tie, having appeared off the bench for Michael Carrick’s side in an August friendly against Atlético Madrid.

JJ Gabriel scored a hat-trick on his last appearance for Manchester United in September before walking out on the club
JJ Gabriel has confirmed his exit from Manchester United with a farewell video message in which he says the club will "will always be part of my story".
The 16-year-old forward, who has a verbal agreement to join Spanish giants Real Madrid, walked out on United in September.
He has subsequently been training on his own in Spain after relocating with his family.
The 50-second video montage, posted on social media, begins with Gabriel penning a letter to United, and includes some of his notable achievements, including coming on for his first-team debut during a pre-season friendly with Atletico Madrid in Stockholm in August, when he was just 15.
Gabriel then thanks United's coaches and staff, plus his team-mates as he "begins my next chapter".
He has not returned to United since scoring a hat-trick in a Uefa Youth League game with Sabah in September.
Although United still hold the teenager's registration until the end of the season, it does not prevent him moving to a club in the European Union as he now has an EU passport through his mother, who is of Cypriot heritage.
Speaking to Spanish newspaper Marca earlier this month, he said his "dream is to win the Ballon d'Or".
However, Gabriel has now broken his silence on his controversial decision to leave United, having won last season's Premier League Under-18 player of the year award, United's U18 player of the year award and been top scorer in a side that reached the FA Youth Cup final and Premier League U18 cup final.
"I arrived in 2020 as a 10-year-old boy with big dreams. Here, I grew as a player and a person, from scoring at Old Trafford to receiving the Jimmy Murphy [Under-18] award . You gave me moments I will always treasure.

Wayne Rooney has revealed there was a period in his Manchester United career where he contemplated taking his own life. The former England striker said that, even as he flourished on the pitch, he was struggling with his mental health off it, despite being newly married and a dad to his eldest child, Kai.
He said he would spend two days at a time drinking at home and, he told the Life At The Midpoint with Gabby Logan podcast, at his lowest point considered taking his own life.
“I can look back and say I was selfish, but I knew I was going through something which I was really struggling to deal with,” Rooney said. “Then I didn’t want Kai seeing me like that, so that’s why I’d hide away as well.
“I got to a place where you’re contemplating suicide. You just didn’t want to be around anyone. I didn’t want to see people in the streets. I didn’t want to go into shops. I was always comfortable on a football pitch, but everything else [I] really struggled with it.”

Match report as Wales lose final Nations League Group A4 game to 10-man Portugal in a 3-2 home defeat; Man Utd's Bruno Fernandes hit opener; Chelsea's Pedro Neto scored Portugal's second but was sent off in second half for two bookings in two minutes; Portugal finish top with Wales bottom
Wales ended their Nations League group campaign with a 3-2 defeat against 10-man Portugal in Cardiff after Chelsea's Pedro Neto was sent off.
Although there was little riding on the contest, with Wales guaranteed a League A relegation/promotion play-off in March and Portugal having qualified for the quarter-finals, the two sides produced an entertaining spectacle.
Portugal skipper Bruno Fernandes blasted the opener after 11 minutes, but that was immediately wiped out by David Brooks' ninth goal for Wales.
Sorba Thomas broke free to put Wales ahead before the break, but again there was a quickfire response as Neto pounced to restore parity.
Substitute Carlos Forbs stroked Portugal ahead in the final quarter, and the visitors had to negotiate the final 16 minutes a player short after Neto was sent off after receiving two yellow cards in the space of two minutes.
Wales finish bottom of League A4 with one win and five defeats, and end a disappointing 2026 with a solitary victory, three draws and six losses from 10 games.
Portugal, meanwhile, finish the campaign as group winners as they earned their first win since Cristiano Ronaldo's international retirement .
Craig Bellamy's side had lost 1-0 in Lisbon in September in a game that was to prove Ronaldo's last for Portugal.
Ronaldo's subsequent retirement from international football probably had an impact on the attendance at Cardiff City Stadium, with some seats unfilled, despite the game being officially declared a sell-out.
There would be no clean sheet for Danny Ward on his 50th appearance as Joao Neves robbed Josh Sheehan and Fernandes lashed home from the edge of the box.
Wales responded immediately with Rubin Colwill twice involved, first setting up Harry Wilson for a shot Diogo Costa blocked with his legs and then Brooks, who swept home his ninth international goal, and second in two games.
Wales hit the front five minutes before the break after Brooks worked a one-two with Wilson before releasing Thomas, who advanced from his own half to slot past Costa.
The lead lasted three minutes as Neto lost Jay DaSilva from Trincao's cross to finish at the far post.
A breathless first half was not finished as Wilson hit the roof of the net from halfway with Costa retreating frantically, and the Leeds midfielder then forced a sprawling save from the Portugal goalkeeper.
Portugal regained the lead 20 minutes from time when Club Brugge winger Forbs - wearing Portugal's new-styled number seven shirt in the post-Ronaldo era - collected Ben Cabango's poor header and stepped inside Ben Davies to find the bottom corner.
Neto clattered into Brennan Johnson just one minute and 59 seconds after being booked, but Portugal held on for a fifth Nations League win to seal top spot.
"We knew in moments we were going to have to suffer due to the quality they have. The intensity wasn't there. We have a lot of players who don't play week in, week out a high-tempo game in such a short space of time. It's not ideal.

"But I know there's more. That's why I wanted to play him in this A league. He's going to have to prove himself."
"For large parts, we played really well again. At times in the first half, we had to suffer. They're a great team full of world-class stars. At times in our shape, we were comfy.

Craig Bellamy's Wales seriously tested reigning Nations League champions Portugal in Cardiff
His Wales side had just lost a fifth game out of six to finish bottom of their Nations League group. Bellamy would have been forgiven for feeling a little bruised.
Wales were fearless against Portugal, exhilarating in attack and proving they can compete at the highest level of this competition, even as they were beaten 3-2 in Cardiff.
And while they were already consigned to the foot of the Group A4 table, Wales' previous performances mean they at least have the back-up of a relegation play-off in March to preserve their top-flight status.
"Belief's the biggest one," Bellamy said when he was asked what he and his team had taken from this campaign.
"Not just this game, but in general. We are beyond close to this level. We can more than compete at this level.
"We demand and want to expect to be. Getting into League A is big for us, but also staying in A is going to allow us to develop.
"You can only develop and improve by playing the best teams, and I felt we've taken another shift."
Former Wales captain Craig Bellamy was appointed head coach in July 2024
Wales have certainly fared better than they did when they were last in the top tier of the Nations League, when they finished with one point from six games and were relegated.
Victory against World Cup quarter-finalists Norway last month was their first at this level and, had they been more clinical in Oslo on Saturday, they might have got a second win of the campaign.
Ultimately, Wales' inability to take their chances – combined with sloppy defensive mistakes – meant their results did not match their performances.
And the reality is that they were up against stellar opposition, whose vastly superior resources showed with their greater ruthlessness at both ends of the pitch.
"If there's anything you would have learned from these games, then you see killers. That's why they're at the top," Bellamy added.
"I know people look at results. I'm fully aware of the business. This is all I know. But I think when you look at reality as well, and you look at our performances during this group, I couldn't ask for more.
"I feel we're closer than probably maybe the players thought they were. It's fine margins.
"But I feel the biggest word out of this now has been belief, really, for me."
Highlights: 10-man Portugal defeat Wales to top Nations League group
Wales had the best record of the four teams who finished bottom of their top-flight groups, meaning they have a second chance to avoid relegation in the form of a two-leg play-off in March.
At Friday's draw in Switzerland, Bellamy's side will discover whether they will face Slovenia, Hungary, Republic of Ireland or Bosnia-Herzegovina, who beat them in a World Cup play-off earlier this year.
Those teams all finished second in their League B groups and, as the League A team, Wales will have home advantage in the second leg.
"Going into the next one, we have to be in this group," said Bellamy. "If we want to develop as a football nation and keep going forward, we have to be playing against the best teams. It's only going to improve you.
"I know we can go back to League B... It's about playing the best teams. That's how we're going to get better. I honestly believe it."
Bellamy, who has a contract running to 2028, said: "I won't be here for the next Nations League. I won't be the manager then. So I'm doing it for the next one, but I'm also doing it for the players.
"We've got to. That's how we're going to be the best version of us and keep improving."

Republic of Ireland vs Kosovo. UEFA Nations League Group B3.
The Republic of Ireland have finished as runners-up in Nations League Group B3; Troy Parrott scored two penalties to send them into the promotion play-offs; the win has also propelled the Euro 2028 co-hosts into a coveted pot-two seeding for next month's qualifying draw
Troy Parrott fired the Republic of Ireland into a Nations League play-off berth with two penalties in their 3-0 victory over 10-man Kosovo at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin.
The result ensured the Republic finished runners-up in group B3, and also propelled the Euro 2028 co-hosts into a coveted pot-two seeding for next month's qualifying draw for that competition.
Tuesday night's contest turned on its head in the 26th minute, when Kreshnik Hajrizi was sent off for handling the ball off the line, and Parrott took advantage with a top-corner finish.
The Real Betis striker doubled the Republic's lead from the spot five minutes after the restart, and Jack Moylan added a 75th-minute cushion to keep alive the hosts' hopes of booking a place in League A for the first time through the March play-off.
Heimir Hallgrimsson's lone change from Saturday's defeat to group winners Austria was the insertion of John Egan into the line-up, replacing injured captain Nathan Collins.
It was a contest that lacked fluidity in the opening 10 minutes, before the Republic found a foothold and Finn Azaz looked to pick out Parrott, but was blocked.
Kosovo then twice missed chances to take the lead. Lindon Emerllahu fired just wide in the 17th minute, and Caoimhin Kelleher was called into action for the first time a minute later to deny Vedat Muriqi.
What had been a largely uneventful encounter suddenly took a dramatic twist in the 26th minute, a red-card incident sparked by Moylan's cross, glanced on by Liam Scales to Parrott.
His effort - clearly goalbound - was cleared off the line by Hajrizi, who extended his arm like a goalkeeper, and was immediately shown a red card by Latvian referee Edgars Malcevs.
Parrott stepped up and gave Arijanet Muric no chance when he rifled into the top right corner to set the Republic on their way.
It remained just a one-goal advantage at the break despite a handful of chances falling the Republic's way, while the visitors created one when Kelleher denied Ilir Krasniqi with 10 minutes remaining to ensure there would be no first-half equaliser.
There was a flurry of Republic chances immediately after the second half kicked off before Parrott added his second penalty.
Muric had just denied Jayson Molumby's effort from range and Parrott was rushing forward to meet the loose ball when he was taken down by the Kosovo keeper.
This time he dove in the right direction, but failed to stop Parrott from doubling the hosts' lead.
The Republic were less successful from open play, unable to put the game away from a string of subsequent chances despite finding themselves in plenty of space, and should have added a third before the hour.
Moylan's persistence finally paid off with 15 minutes remaining, nodding home substitute Liam Kitching's cross in off the post.
The Republic nearly added a late fourth when Adam Idah stung the palms of Muric with two minutes left.
Republic of Ireland striker Troy Parrott speaking to RTÉ about the 2028 Euros:
"I've been thinking about it since I was a kid, I think everyone has.
"Look, it's not a guarantee that we are going to qualify for that tournament, so I think tonight was very important to get into pot two so that we have a better draw.
"We'll be going into the qualifiers now, trying to make sure that we qualify for the tournament.
"A tournament that's one of the host nations being Ireland, without Ireland it would be heartbreaking for all of us, so I think it's a mission now to make sure that we're there.
"It was disappointing that we didn't win the group because that's what we all wanted to do at the start.
"There's been so many nearly matches where we've nearly won, we've played really well and haven't won, and I think tonight we went out there with the mindset that no matter what we have to win.
"Obviously the red card helped us, but I have no doubt in my mind that group of players who were out on that pitch would have won that game."
Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson speaking at his post-match press conference:
"Everybody, and especially us, likes to play the top teams. To compare yourself with the best teams, that's one thing.
"Second is those teams will expose your weaknesses, and that helps you in your growth to play these teams, so we can continue our growth.
"We're already looking forward to March. Tough teams in the pot. Whoever we draw is going to be a tough two games, and it's good for this team at this time to play these matches instead of friendlies.
"We're really excited for March, and looking forward to meeting the players again."

A year and a day on from his hat-trick in Budapest which helped Republic of Ireland snatch a dramatic 3-2 win over Hungary to make the World Cup play-offs, Troy Parrott scored another two big goals to help the Irish to a 3-0 win over Kosovo in the Nations League.
His two penalties set Heimir Hallgrimsson's side on their way to a much-needed victory as they secured second spot in Group B3 - which brings with it a place in pot two for the Euro 2028 qualifying draw and a Nations League play-off with the chance to go up to League A for the first time.
The two strikes brought Parrott's tally for his country up to 17 in 43 caps.
Twelve of those goals have come in his past nine competitive appearances, with six in his past three games at the Aviva Stadium.
The past 12 months have been transformative for Parrott, who also earned a move to Real Betis in the summer after starring for AZ Alkmaar.
He has since scored against Real Madrid and in the Champions League for Betis alongside establishing himself as Republic of Ireland's talisman.
He will carry their hopes of qualifying for Euro 2028, just as his idol and the country's all-time leading scorer Robbie Keane did for many years when he led the line.
While he has taken an arduous route to the top, Parrott is content he is finally fulfilling his potential at club level and on the international stage.
"Growing up watching Robbie Keane, he was the main man and it's always what I wanted to do. I've worked really hard to get here and now I'm in a really good spot," he told RTE.
"Professional football is one of the hardest professions to make it in, so many people want to be a footballer. If I didn't have a stronger mentality, I could have failed.
"Now I am at the level that I always knew I could get to and there are more levels to come. I am really excited for it."
Republic of Ireland finished their Nations League campaign with two wins, two draws and two defeats from their six games.
The two victories were highlights of what was a testing campaign on and off the pitch because of the decision to go ahead with two games against Israel.
The controversy surrounding the first Israel game in particular - which the Irish ended up winning 3-0 in Debrecen - was difficult for the squad to navigate.
The match looked in doubt the previous day when training was delayed as players took a vote on whether to play - amid protests over the Israel-Gaza war - with goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu making himself unavailable for selection.
Parrott reiterated the point that Dara O'Shea and Nathan Collins made earlier in the week, that the collective group of players are stronger coming out the other side of it all.
"It was very difficult the last camp with all the pressure on us as players, it was a bit of a strange one because no-one has experienced anything like that before - players, staff or the FAI - so it was strange and a bit difficult," he said.
"It was important for us because people had to come out of their shells and give opinions, the quiet ones had to have a voice in the changing room so it was good everyone came together.
"When we played Israel in the away game the performance symbolised everything we went through in the week, we came out and destroyed them."
Republic of Ireland will face a League A side in March's two-legged play-off for the chance to reach the top tier for the first time
Republic of Ireland had many "nearly" moments in the group, from the late narrow defeats in Pristina and Linz to the frustration of being pegged back by Israel and Austria in draws when they were ahead.
The pressure was on for them to deliver in their must-win game against Kosovo on Tuesday and they did, comfortably.
Although aided by the red card shown to Kreshnik Hajrizi, Parrott believes they would have still won had Kosovo had 11 men on the pitch and was relieved they could demonstrate again, as they did against Portugal and Hungary last year, that they can win when it matters.
Moving up to pot two for next month's Euro 2028 draw should, in theory, present the Irish with a kinder draw for a tournament they are desperate to qualify for, given the Aviva Stadium will host some games.
"We felt and everyone else felt we could have won this group but the most important thing is getting into that pot two. It was a big game for us, it wasn't a nearly game we went out and done it so it's a credit to everyone.
"It's disappointing we didn't win the group because that's what we wanted to do at the start. There's been so many nearly matches where we have nearly won or played well and haven't won and I think tonight we went out there with the mindset no matter what, we had to win.
"It's not guaranteed that we will qualify [for the Euros] so it was important to get pot two to get a better draw and we'll be going to the qualifiers hoping to qualify. A tournament hosted by Ireland without Ireland in it would be heart-breaking, so that's our mission to make sure we're there."
Before attentions turns to Euro 2028 qualifying, Republic of Ireland will take on a League A side over two legs in March's Nations League play-off as they try to reach the top tier for the first time.
Parrott's focus between now and March is clear, getting back to Seville and "putting the ball in the back of the net" for Real Betis as he has done so well for Republic of Ireland in the past year.

Nations League quarter-finals, semi-finals and final format explained, with draw for last eight on Friday after groups decided; England had already progressed to knockouts but won group with victory over Spain in Madrid on Sunday
England have topped their group in the Nations League after an incredible win over Spain - but who will they play in the last eight in March?
England's win over Spain in Madrid means they have finished top of the group.
That matters as the winners of the Nations League tier A groups are seeded for the quarter-final draw. They will play teams which have finished runners-up in other groups. They will also play the second leg of their quarter-final at home.
Belgium finished runners-up in Group A1, so they are a potential last-eight opponent for England.
Netherlands are another potential opponent as they finished second in Group A2 following their 5-0 loss to Germany, who topped the group.
Norway are the final team after they came from 2-0 down to beat Denmark 3-2 - and qualify for the quarter-finals at the Dane's expense.
The Three Lions cannot draw Spain in the quarters, as teams from the same group cannot face each other in the quarters, or France because they finished as Group A1 winners.
The draw for the last eight will take place on Friday at 11am UK time.
The quarter-finals will be two-leg ties, with the seeded group winners playing the second match at home.
The matches will take place in the March international break, with the first legs between March 25-27 and the second legs between March 28-30.
The Nations League Finals will then be held between June 9 and June 13, 2027.
The tournament will feature two semi-finals, a third-place play-off and the final, with four nations competing to be crowned champions of Europe.
The four semi-finalists will be invited to make bids to host the semi-finals and final.

Wayne Rooney has revealed he considered taking his own life while playing for Manchester United; this article discusses mental health and suicide, which some readers may find distressing; if you have been affected by this story, support and guidance are available at sky.com/viewersupport
Wayne Rooney has revealed there was a period in his Manchester United career where he contemplated suicide.
The former England striker revealed that, despite enjoying success on the pitch, he was struggling with his mental health off it. Newly married and a father to eldest son Kai, Rooney would sometimes spend two days drinking at home.
Speaking on the Life at the Midpoint with Gabby Logan podcast, he admitted that, at his lowest point, he had contemplated taking his own life.
"I can look back and say I was selfish, but I knew I was going through something which I was really struggling to deal with. Then I didn't want Kai seeing me like that, so that's why I'd hide away as well," Rooney said.
"I got to a place where you're contemplating suicide. You just didn't want to be around anyone. I didn't want to be see people in the streets. I didn't want to go into shops.
"I was always comfortable on a football pitch, but everything else [I] really struggled with it."
Rooney, United's all-time record goalscorer, said the issues he faced occurred at the height of his Red Devils career.
"You don't want to show any weakness, so you try to mask it," he added.
"Even though I knew the position I was in, it was difficult to actually admit that I was in that in that position because I felt like you feel less of a man if you like for doing that.
"I was speaking to a therapist to try and figure out what was up with me because when I look back I was probably at the height of my career, I've just had a young son, I've just been married. It should be the happiest point in my life and it wasn't.
"It was probably the lowest point because of the selfish acts I was taking."
Rooney, who is currently featuring in ITV reality programme 'I'm A Celebrity… Get Me Out Of Here', credits his wife Coleen with helping him turn the tide.
"Coleen helped me massively. She could have walked away, it was that bad, but she stuck by me and helped me get through it," he said.

England could host the Nations League finals this season after Football Association officials registered their interest.
The semi-final and finals of the competition, due to take place in June, are held in one country.
As well as England, it is understood that Spain and France have also contacted Uefa to register their interest in hosting the final four games, including the bronze medal match, which will run between 9-13 June.
The FA, it is understood, is still discussing potential venues with some doubt over whether Wembley would be available. The only publicly announced Wembley events in June are two concerts by singer Sam Fender, although these are for after the Nations League.
Since the tournament began in 2019, England have never held the finals, with Portugal, Italy, Netherlands and Germany the hosts to date.
Generally, only nations who reach the last four of the Nations League are considered to host the latter stages.
Thomas Tuchel's team will be seeded in Friday's draw for the quarter-finals following their euphoric 3-2 victory over Spain in Madrid, which secured top place in the group.
They could face Belgium, Netherlands, Denmark or Norway in March in the next round before June's finals.
If the FA's bid is successful, it will provide the governing body with an opportunity to host a mini-tournament before Euro 2028, which will be held in England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland.

Arsenal have paid tribute to Peter Storey, a key member of their 1971 Double-winning team, after the death of the former England midfielder at the age of 81.
Storey was part of the Bertie Mee team that secured the First Division title and FA Cup in a season that remains one of the most celebrated in Arsenal’s history and played 501 times for the club. That places him eighth on their appearances list.
Storey, who represented England on 19 occasions from 1971-73, earned respect for his uncompromising approach and versatility, also featuring at right-back.
Storey died in hospital after a short illness, surrounded by his family. Arsenal said: “Everyone at Arsenal is deeply saddened by the passing of 1970-71 Double winner Peter Storey. All our thoughts are with his family and loved ones at this incredibly sad time.”
Born in Surrey, Storey began his career at Arsenal and made his debut shortly after his 20th birthday in 1965. He is fondly remembered by the club’s fans for scoring a stoppage-time penalty in the 1971 FA Cup semi-final against Stoke that forced a replay and kept the Double dream alive.
Storey left for Fulham in 1977 and retired eight months later when his contract was cancelled, going on to own a pub in north London. He was later convicted of several criminal offences, including financing a plot to counterfeit gold coins and smuggling pornography. He released an autobiography , True Storey: My Life and Crimes as a Football Hatchet Man, in September 2010.
Storey’s family said: “We are deeply grateful for the many kind messages, tributes and good wishes we have received. It has been a great comfort to see the affection and respect in which he was held by so many, both within the football community and beyond.”

Swansea boss Vitor Matos spent five years on Jurgen Klopp's staff at Liverpool
Vitor Matos is on the brink of leaving Swansea City to take charge of French top-flight club Strasbourg.
Matos, 38, is understood to have said goodbye to players and staff at the Swans' Fairwood training base on Tuesday after Strasbourg made an official approach for the Swansea head coach.
There is no confirmation yet that a deal has been agreed between the clubs, but Strasbourg are thought to be ready to pay in the region of £5m to secure the Portuguese's services.
News of Strasbourg's interest had emerged on Monday, with Matos - who is under contract at Swansea until 2030 - telling the Championship club he wanted to leave.
Four members of Matos' coaching team - Diogo Medeiros, Toze Mendes, Goncalo Ricca and head of goalkeeping Pedro Pereira - are also expected to depart.
That will leave Swansea stalwarts Leon Britton and Kristian O'Leary as the only remaining senior staff members at the club heading into Saturday's home game against West Bromwich Albion.
Matos had been due to celebrate a year in charge at Swansea later this month.
Current Strasbourg boss Hugo Oliveira, Matos' fellow countryman, has been under pressure after a run of five defeats in six matches.
Oliveira has managed only three wins in 10 league games since succeeding Gary O'Neil - who left to take over at Ipswich Town – in July.
O'Neil led Strasbourg to an eighth-place finish last season, but they are currently 13th in Ligue 1, only two points above the relegation zone.
Strasbourg are a sister club of Premier League side Chelsea.
Matos has turned Swansea from potential relegation contenders to promotion hopefuls since taking charge, with the club 20th in the Championship when he took over last November.
The Swans finished 11th last season and have made further strides in the first third of this campaign.
Vitor Matos led Swansea to seven wins in their first 10 league games of the season, though they have since lost four in five
Matos' team have been among the early-season pacesetters in the second tier, enjoying two spells on top of the table, but their form has dipped in recent weeks.
Swansea have suffered four defeats in their past five matches, though they remain only three points off top spot before West Brom's visit.
Matos was touted as a contender to take charge at Crystal Palace earlier this season - the Eagles have since appointed Thomas Frank - while he has also been linked with a return to Portugal on the back of his impact at Swansea.
When asked in October about the Palace links, Matos said: "I'm Swansea manager. I love being here, love my players, love the staff, so my focus is always on the next game and what we can do better."
In an interview last week, Swansea chief executive Tom Gorringe acknowledged that Matos' impact will not have gone unnoticed at other clubs, though he played down the idea of the former Liverpool coach having his head turned.
"The reality is there'll always be interest in anyone performing well in any role on and off the pitch," Gorringe said.
"That's one of the outcomes of being successful - we're aware of that.
"[But] we're all quite happy. We've all agreed to go on this journey together and we hope that Vitor is here a long time."
After meeting West Brom, who are fifth in the second tier, sixth-placed Swansea go to second-placed Middlesbrough next Tuesday.
They then host Cardiff City in the first south Wales derby in two seasons on Sunday, 29 November.
Vitor Matos latest: Strasbourg close in on Swansea head coach
Vitor Matos is relatively inexperienced if you look at his senior management experience alone, but his wealth of footballing experience is evident when taking a wider look at his footballing journey.
Speaking to BBC Sport earlier this season, Matos explained how his 23 years in football have informed his development - a journey that began when a 15-year-old Matos was inspired by Jose Mourinho's Champions League triumph with Porto.
So, although he only took his first managerial job at the start of last season in the second division of Portugal, to call Matos an overnight success story would be false.
He developed an understanding of positional play while working as a youth coach at FC Porto, before moving to China. As technical director and an under-16 coach of Shandong Taishan, he added layers of knowledge to his positional game:
"In China, I understood that to arrive at a more positional game, you could have different steps beforehand," he explained.
"There is a benefit to having more players close to each other, rather than spreading them over space.
"If you spread them over space, you are demanding that, technically, they can solve many situations one-v-one. If they come closer to the ball, you can generate more possibilities. You can create a tempo that allows other players to be better in the big spaces."
The uniqueness of these overloads, around the ball, have been a hallmark of some of Swansea's impressive attacking play this season.
Following stints in Portugal and China, he then found himself working alongside Jurgen Klopp and Pep Lijnders at Liverpool, which provided him a greater understanding of senior football at the elite level.
"Liverpool influenced me a lot in terms of counter-pressing, pressing, intensity, and what makes you grow as a team," he said.
"The most important thing is how much you believe in your idea, and this style is how I see football. That's why I want this to be the foundation for our team."

Real Madrid'in 21 yaşındaki yıldızı Arda Güler için Paris Saint-Germain'in 200 milyon euroluk teklif hazırladığı iddia edildi. Böyle bir satış gerçekleşirse Fenerbahçe , bonservisten kalan yüzde 20'lik pay sayesinde kasasına yaklaşık 40 milyon euro koyacak.
İspanyol El Gol Digital'in haberine göre Fransa 'nın en büyük kulübü, Real Madrid'in genç orta sahasını kadrosuna katmak için 200 milyon euroluk bir teklifi masaya koymaya hazırlanıyor.
Dikkat çeken ikinci detay zamanlama. İddiaya göre Real Madrid ile Güler yeni sözleşme konusunda anlaşamazsa, PSG'nin teklifi kış transfer dönemine doğru çok daha ciddi bir hal alacak. 21 yaşındaki oyuncunun Madrid'deki geleceği, bu yüzden önümüzdeki haftaların en çok konuşulan transfer başlıklarından biri olmaya aday.
Maaş tarafındaki fark da büyük. Real Madrid'in Güler'e yıllık 8 milyon euroluk yeni bir sözleşme önerdiği, oyuncunun bu teklife henüz olumlu yanıt vermediği öne sürülüyor. PSG'nin ise yıllık 22 milyon euro ödemeyi göze aldığı iddia ediliyor. Yani iki teklif arasında yılda 14 milyon euroluk bir uçurum var.
Real Madrid cephesinden gelen haberler ise tek bir yöne işaret etmiyor. Ekim ayında Mundo Deportivo, Fabrizio Romano'ya dayandırdığı haberinde 2032'ye kadar uzatma anlaşmasının tamamlandığını yazmıştı. AS'den José Félix Díaz ise kulübün 2031'e kadar bir yenileme üzerinde çalıştığını aktarmıştı. Güler'in 8 milyon euroluk teklifi reddettiği bilgisi ise ESPN'e atfedildi.
Fenerbahçe 'nin bu hikâyedeki payı, 2023 yazında imzalanan transfer anlaşmasından geliyor. Güler, o dönem Real Madrid'e 20 milyon euro artı 10 milyon euro bonus olmak üzere toplam 30 milyon euroluk bonservis bedeliyle gitmiş, 6 yıllık sözleşme imzalamıştı. Sarı-lacivertliler anlaşmaya ileride yapılacak satıştan yüzde 20 pay alacakları maddesini de eklemişti.
Hesap basit: 200 milyon euroluk bir satışta bu oran 40 milyon euroya karşılık geliyor. Mayıs ayında yayımlanan bir habere göre 90 milyon euroluk bir satışta bile Fenerbahçe'nin payı yaklaşık 18 milyon euro olacaktı. Yani 2023'te kasaya giren paranın üzerine, aradan geçen yıllarda çok daha büyük bir ek gelir ihtimali doğdu.
Transfer iddialarının ortasında Güler'in sahadaki rakamları da dikkat çekiyor. 21 yaşındaki oyuncu, 2026/27 sezonunda Real Madrid formasıyla tüm kulvarlarda 14 maça çıktı, 4 gol attı ve 7 asist yaptı. Yani maç başına yarımdan fazla gol katkısı üretiyor.
Madrid yönetiminin 8 milyon euroluk yenileme teklifine henüz yanıt alamadığı, PSG'nin ise yıllık 22 milyon euroluk bir maaş paketiyle devreye girmeye hazırlandığı konuşuluyor. Güler ile Real Madrid arasındaki sözleşme görüşmelerinin kış transfer dönemine kadar sonuçlanıp sonuçlanmayacağı bekleniyor.

Declan Rice has agreed a new long term-contract at Arsenal so can he continue to go from strength to strength? Jack Wilshere, his former team-mate at West Ham, tells Sky Sports Rice is "definitely in the conversation as one of the best midfielders in the world"
Arsenal's Kroenke family owners tend not to get involved in transfer dealings. But when it came to Declan Rice, and the prospect of spending £100m on a player for the first time, they needed to be sure that it was a sensible investment.
So, in the conference room at Arsenal's training ground, co-chair Josh Kroenke asked to be walked through the deal by Mikel Arteta, former sporting director Edu, then executive vice-chair Tim Lewis and now chief executive officer Richard Garlick.
"My eyebrows raised because I didn't know if we were in that phase just yet to go after a player like that," Kroenke recalled. He wanted to know what he would bring and how Arteta would use him.
Kroenke left the meeting in no doubt about the deal, either financially or in footballing terms. A club-record approach to West Ham was greenlit and Rice has of course gone on to prove an inspired addition, his new deal reflecting his importance.
"Declan Rice, we got him half price," is the refrain among Arsenal supporters. A player instrumental in their Premier League title success, who insisted "it's not done", then did more than anyone to drive them over the line, is now tied down for his peak years.
He has brought Arsenal even more than the club anticipated, arriving as a No 6 before being unshackled as a rampaging No 8, then reverting to a deeper role this season.
He scores, creates and dominates physically. His deadly set-piece delivery, honed to a world-class level, is another weapon.
"He is becoming a total player," said Arteta, who has even called on him at right-back. Of course, Rice filled in admirably in that role. "A total player has to be able to do as many things as possible and he has the capacity to do that," added Arteta.
Rice's adaptability and willingness to evolve his game have been themes of his time at Arsenal. The same traits were apparent to those who worked with him at West Ham, where he made an instant impression on his former team-mate Jack Wilshere.
"I love Declan, first of all a person," Wilshere tells Sky Sports. "I could see that straight away when I went in. He was very humble, his eyes were open, he wanted to learn, he would ask the right questions, and he just went from strength to strength.
"His footballing ability speaks for itself, but I wouldn't say he's someone who it came naturally to. He had to work on his right foot, on his left foot. But physically, he was always a beast and that would help him get out of certain situations."
Wilshere also noted the leadership qualities that have come to the fore at Arsenal. "Even when I went there and he was 19 or 20 and finding his way in the team, he had natural leadership and a natural aura about him that you could see," he says.
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
"He has a good understanding as well. When you look at players making big moves now, for me, one of the most important things around it is timing. I think Dec got his timing right.
"He spent a good few years at West Ham becoming a hero, becoming an important member of that team, trying to get that team up the table to finish high as possible. He won a trophy with them, and then he decided to go and compete for bigger things."
Wilshere and Rice crossed paths again following his move to Arsenal, where Wilshere, now head coach of Luton Town, was working as an academy coach and shadowing his old team-mate Arteta.
"I know how important he was to Mikel at that time when Mikel brought him in, and how he was going to be that shining light of the team who would always be present," he says.
"That's another thing that's really impressive about him: his robustness. He plays every single game. He dominates every single game physically."
Rice's record bears it out. Last season was his most demanding yet as he made 55 appearances in all competitions for Arsenal, many of them while managing hamstring nerve pain, before making a further eight for England at the World Cup during the summer.
He is an incredible athlete who continues to show remarkable resistance to injury. He has only missed five out of 119 Premier League games since his arrival at Arsenal. Only four outfield players have played more minutes in the competition in that timeframe.
His reliability is invaluable to Arteta and Rice continues to find ways to improve. Having moved back to the base of midfield this term, switching to the right side of the pivot to accommodate Myles Lewis-Skelly and Bruno Guimaraes, he has become notably more incisive with his passes.
His total of five assists is the highest of any Premier League player this season and it is notable that all of them have come in open-play.
According to Opta, Rice ranks second among Premier League players - and top among midfielders - for line-breaking passes this season, behind only Jan Paul van Hecke. He also ranks second only to Martin Odegaard for line-breaking passes in the final third.
A player once criticised for sideways passing is now averaging nearly twice as many line-breaking passes than last season, showing clear development in yet another area of his game.
The hope for Arsenal is that Rice will continue to unlock more levels after committing his future to the club. That is certainly the expectation from those who know him.
"I actually think there's more to come from Dec," adds Wilshere. "I've said it for a few years now. To be fair, he has started to add goals, but I still think he can add more with his physical ability, with his ability to strike the ball off his left foot, right foot.
"But he's already a top player and definitely in the conversation as one of the best midfielders in the world."

Wayne Rooney says he was "contemplating suicide" during his playing days at Manchester United and was "speaking to a therapist to try and figure out what was up".
The former England captain joined United from Everton in 2004 and went on to become the club's record goalscorer, with 253 goals in 559 appearances.
But Rooney, speaking with Gabby Logan on the Life at the Midpoint podcast , external , detailed his struggles off the pitch when eldest son Kai, who is now 17, was a baby.
"When I was drinking, I would lock myself in my house for two days and just drink," said Rooney, when asked about the lowest point in his life.
"This is probably in my best part of my career playing wise."
The 41-year-old went on to explain how he "struggled to deal with it all" and, after opening up to his wife Coleen and his mother, knew he "needed help to get through it".
"I can look back and say I was selfish, but I knew I was going through something which I was really struggling to deal with," he added.
"I didn't want Kai seeing me like that, so that's why I'd hide away as well.
"I got to a place where you're contemplating suicide. I just didn't want to be around anyone. I didn't want to see people in the streets. I didn't want to go into shops.
"I was always comfortable on a football pitch, but everything else, [I] really struggled with it."
Rooney, who scored 53 goals in 120 England appearances, was recently named pundit of the year at the Broadcast Sport Awards and is currently appearing on reality TV show I'm a Celebrity... Get Me Out of Here.
He helped United win five Premier League titles, the Champions League, Europa League, FA Cup and three EFL Cups before leaving them to return to the Toffees in 2017.
But the former forward said he learned to mask his feelings during his lowest moments.
"You don't want to show any weakness, so you try to mask it," Rooney added.
"Even though I knew the position I was in, it was difficult to actually admit that I was in that position because I felt like you feel less of a man, if you like, for doing that.
"I was speaking to a therapist to try and figure out what was up with me because when I look back I was probably at the height of my career, I've just had a young son, I've just been married.
"It was probably the lowest point because of the selfish acts I was taking.
"Coleen helped me massively. She could have walked away, it was that bad, but she stuck by me and helped me get through it."

İstanbul'daki bir otelde yapılan toplantının ardından Kulüpler Birliği Vakfı Başkanı Ertuğrul Doğan, basın mensuplarının sorularını yanıtladı.
Toplantıdan önce gerçekleştirilen, Kulüpler Birliği Vakfının düzenlediği "Futbol Zirvesi" programına ilişkin emeği geçenlere teşekkür eden Doğan, "Kulüpler Birliği olarak içeride birçok konu konuşuldu ama iki konu hakkında bazı şeyler söylemek istiyorum. Birincisi naklen yayın ihalesi. Kulüplerimizin beklentisi, daha önce Sayın Göksel Gümüşdağ zamanında gelen 500 milyon dolar seviyesine yeniden gelmek. Bunun altını çiziyoruz. Kulüplerin mali sıkıntıları çok büyük ve bu rakamları görmemiz gerektiğini düşünüyoruz. Bunu öncelikle belirteyim." diye konuştu.
Rekabet ortamını artıran firmalara da teşekkür eden Doğan, şöyle devam etti:
“Turkcell'e teşekkür ediyorum. Rekabet ortamının oluşturulması konusunda çok önemli çalışmaları oldu. Sayın Şenol Kazancı ve ekibine teşekkür ederim, sağ olsunlar. İhaleye ciddi bir rekabeti getireceklerini biliyoruz artık. Son olarak da vergi konularıyla alakalı konuşmak istiyorum. Her kulübümüzün ciddi anlamda mali sıkıntılarının olduğu bir gerçek, bunu hepiniz biliyorsunuz. Bu konuda bir açıklamamız olacak. Vergi oranlarının çok yüksek olduğunu düşünüyoruz. İkinci konumuz vergi iadesi, yani stopaj konusu aslında. Biliyorsunuz bu stopaj amatör sporlar için çok önemli, olmazsa olmazı. Dört büyük kulüp dahil olmak üzere tüm kulüplerimiz bunun üzerinden faaliyetlerine devam edebiliyor. Sayın Cumhurbaşkanımızın sağ olsun yıllar önce kulüplerimize yaptığı bir jest bu. Sayın Cumhurbaşkanımızın talimatlarıyla yapılmıştı. Biz en son yaptığımız görüşmelerde konuyu kendisine aktarmıştık. Biz yine kulüpler olarak Sayın Cumhurbaşkanımızdan randevu isteyeceğiz bu stopaj konusunda çünkü azalan rakamlar söz konusu. Oransal anlamda bunun yeniden eski haline getirilmesi konusunda Sayın Cumhurbaşkanımızdan ricacı olacağız. Önümüzdeki günlerde de kendisinden randevu isteyip hep beraber gideceğiz.”
Kulüpler olarak yayın gelirinde maksimum faydayı gözettiklerini aktaran Doğan, "Kulüpler Birliği olarak düşüncemiz, maksimum faydayı sağlayabilmek. Çünkü tüm kulüplerimiz mali olarak ciddi anlamda sıkıntı çekiyor. Bu bir gerçek, bunu da Türkiye'deki herkes biliyor artık. Dolayısıyla naklen yayın ihalesi bizim açımızdan çok önemli. Kulüplerin bu rakamlarda durulması konusunda ciddi talebi var, ortak talebi var. Herkesin görüşü ve düşüncesi net olarak bu yönde." değerlendirmesinde bulundu.
Kulüplerden bazı konularda geri dönüşler alacaklarını anlatan Doğan, şunları kaydetti:
“Şimdi biz bugün itibarıyla belli konular hakkında kulüplerimizin geri dönüşünü alacağız. Kulüpler Birliğinde bizim bir ihale komisyonumuz var, sürekli olarak bunu her gün kendi aramızda konuşuyoruz. Yani Kulüpler Birliği olarak bakmayın, içinde bir yayın grubu var bunun. Naklen yayın ihaleleriyle alakalı bir grubumuz var. Dört büyük kulüp var orada, Göksel Bey var aynı zamanda, Göztepe var, vesaire. Bu arkadaşlarla sürekli konuşuyoruz. Oluşan her konu hakkında hem federasyon hem de ihaleye gelecek olan firmalarla yaptığımız görüşmeler oluyor. Onları da bilgilendiriyoruz. Dolayısıyla önümüzdeki bir hafta, on gün içerisinde bunlar daha sıklıkla devam edecektir ama toplu olarak bir Kulüpler Birliği toplantısı gibi olmayabilir çünkü zaman çok az. Ama naklen yayın grubu ve komisyonu bu arada tekrar görüşecektir.”
Yayın kalitesinin artması yönündeki çalışmalara da değinen Doğan, şöyle konuştu:
“Biz bu konuda çok önemli bir çalışma yaptık. Çok değerli kurumlardan, firmalardan görüşler aldık. Rapor haline getirdik. Federasyonumuza da olması gerektiği şekilde sunduk. Ama sizlerle de paylaşalım, Kulüpler Birliğinin yaptığı çalışmayı görmüş olursunuz. Zaman zaman bunlar hep buranın gündemine geldi. Ama bir oluşum sağlanamadı. Sağlanamamasının arkasında belli sebepler var, kanuni sebepler de var arkasında. Bu tek başına Kulüpler Birliğinin şu anda karar verip uygulayabileceği bir konu değil. Ama ben her alanda profesyonelleşmenin başarı getirdiğine inanan biriyim. Dolayısıyla bu alanda çok ciddi çalışma yapılması şarttır ve gerekliliktir benim görüşüm olarak. Ama bununla alakalı Kulüpler Birliği çalışma yapacak, onu gereklilikleriyle paylaşacağız. Yani kanunlar gereği şu anda tek başımıza bizim böyle bir şirket kurup bu hakları verin diyeceğimiz bir durum yok. Bunlar yapılır mı, değiştirilebilir mi, her şey olabilir. Konuşulması gereken bir şey ama bu da çok önemli bir soru. Çünkü marka değeri ancak böyle gelişiyor. Yani bunun başka bir alternatifi yok veya bu işi yöneten arkadaşlarımızın çok daha detaylı çalışmalarla bu işin içerisinde olması gerekiyor. Bundan başka bir çare yok.”
Yayın gelirlerini görüşmelerle artırdıklarını anlatan Ertuğrul Doğan, şunları aktardı:
“Kulüpler Birliği olarak bu konuyla ilgili ilk konuşmaya başladığımız zamanla geldiğimiz nokta arasında çok ciddi fark var, pozitif anlamda. Ama bizim istediğimiz yere kadar da bir yol olduğu gerçek. İnşallah bundan sonrası da yine istediğimiz şekilde planlanır, gelişir ve kulüpler ciddi bir gelir kalemine sahip olur. Çünkü altını çizerek söylüyorum, bu gelirlerle bu kulüplerin yaşama şansı çok zor. Bunun dışında asıl önemli konu da biraz önce belirttiğim konu, stopaj konusu. Former Arsenal and England midfielder Peter Storey has died at the age of 81.
Storey made 501 appearances in all competitions for the Gunners between 1965 and 1977, scoring 17 goals.
He was part of the Double-winning Arsenal team which secured the First Division title and FA Cup in 1970-71 under manager Bertie Mee.
"Everyone at Arsenal is deeply saddened by the passing of double winner Peter Storey," Arsenal said in a statement.
"All our thoughts are with his family and loved ones at this incredibly sad time.

Surrey-born Storey joined Arsenal as an apprentice in 1961 and made his first-team debut against Leicester City in 1965, initially starting his career at right-back before being moved into midfield.
He is currently eighth on Arsenal 's list of all-time appearance holders and was capped 19 times by England, although he did not feature in a major tournament for the Three Lions.
Storey collected runners-up medals with Arsenal in the League Cup in 1967-68 and 1968-69 and in the FA Cup in 1971-72.
He joined Second Division Fulham on a free transfer in March 1977 and made 19 appearances for the Cottagers before his contract was terminated later that year and he retired.
However, Storey had something of a troubled life after his retirement from professional football.
He was convicted of running a brothel - for which he received a suspended prison sentence in 1979 - and was later jailed for three years for his involvement in a counterfeiting operation, then served another prison sentence in 1990 for attempting to smuggle pornographic videos into Britain.
